processinfo.head: Processing Information

p.emph: Starting in 2023, Library of Virginia archival staff in partnership with the Virginia Untold Project Manager began efforts to describe records related to free and enslaved Black and Multiracial people in a manner that improved the historical context of the records. In doing so, in some cases material once described within the "Free and Enslaved" record group for a locality may no longer be described within this record. When this has occurred, please see the Processing Information and Related Materials section for records that have been described separately.

processinfo.p: "Free Negro" Registrations, 1805, 1813-1828, undated were removed from this record in July 2026 and are now described in Sussex County (Va.) Records Related to the Registration of Free Persons.
"Free Negro" Register, 1800-1850, removed from this record in July 2026 and are now described in Sussex County (Va.) Records Related to the Registration of Free Persons.

bioghist.head: Historical Information
bioghist.p: The Free and Enslaved Records collection is comprised of miscellaneous records related to the regulation and policing of both enslaved and free Black and Multiracial people in Bedford County. The localities/local government authorities were largely responsible for enforcing laws that restricted the movement of enslaved and free Black and Multiracial people and the resulting documentation was often filed in the circuit courts. The ways in which local authorities enacted legal measures against or on behalf of enslaved and free Black and Multiracial people varied from locality to locality; therefore, records were not necessarily standardized or filed and retained in a consistent manner. This collection is topical and a means by which to compile miscellaneous documents related to free and enslaved people that are not established local government record types.
See: the Virginia Untold Record Types on the Library of Virginia website for additional context concerning "Free Negro" Tax Records
Locality History:Sussex County was named for the English county, and was formed from Surry County by a statute adopted in 1753. The county court first met on 30 May 1754.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content
scopecontent.p: Sussex County (Va.) Free and Enslaved Records, 1787-1821, are comprised of deeds of emancipation, 1787-1788; "Free Negro" Tax Records, 1801-1812; and lists of individuals enslaved by dower estates, 1804-1821.

Deeds of emancipation, 1787-1788, document the emancipation of people enslaved by Henry Moss and Henry Porch. Enslaved names include Beck, Phebe, Pat, Oney, Bob, Anothony, West, Sam, Edrige, Hall. [Sussex County Reel no. 319]

"Free Negro" tax records consist of 23 "List of Free Negroes and Mulattoes," 1801-1834, created by Commissioners of revenue in each tax district for tax purposes. These lists note the name of the individual along with their sex, occupation, and residence. [digital images]

Estate documents concerning the division of persons enslaved by various dower estates, 1804-1821. These include the dower estates of Lucy Dunn , Amy Hunt, P. Hunnicutt, Mary Tomlinson, Elizabeth Burdge, Elizabeth Ruffin, Lucy Seammell, and Elizabeth Rose. These records are comprised of nine lists of enslaved people who were acquired through marriage to a widow who had inherited them as part of her dower. Many of the lists document the names, sex, and age of the enslaved people. [Sussex County Reel no. 319]

Additional Sussex County (Va.) Court Records can be found on microfilm at The Library of Virginia web site. Consult "A Guide to Virginia County and City Records on Microfilm."
